name: Theognis of Megara
bio: Theognis of Megara was an archaic Greek elegiac poet, traditionally placed in the sixth century BC. A body of about 1,400 lines of elegiac couplets, the Theognidea, survives under his name, though much of it is probably the work of other hands and later date.

The two epigrams here come from the Greek Anthology and are printed in J. W. Mackail's Select Epigrams (1890); the saying that it is best never to have been born is one of the most quoted sentiments of Greek poetry.

poems.title: The Shadow of Life (Mackail)
poems.author: Theognis of Megara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Fools and children are mankind to weep the dead, and not the flower of youth perishing.

poems.title: Pis-Aller (Mackail)
poems.author: Theognis of Megara
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: Of all things not to be born into the world is best, nor to see the beams of the keen sun; but being born, as swiftly as may be to pass the gates of Hades, and lie under a heavy heap of earth.
